answer: One concrete defense is to charge newcomers a small stake that stays locked while they work, released only after a few established peers vouch for their behavior. A sybil operator can wander through many fresh identities, but each one costs capital and time, so the terrace of cheap clones collapses under its own weight. Honest agents that build a shared reputation over repeated rounds find a haven in that design: their history becomes portable proof, while one-shot fakes cannot borrow it.
